episodeTitle.en: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more
episodeTitle.zh: 杰森·弗里德挑战您对融资、目标、增长等的认知

guestBioOfficial.en: Jason Fried is the co-founder and CEO of 37signals, the maker of Basecamp and HEY. 37signals is a very different kind of company. With fewer than 80 employees, they have over 100,000 customers, generate tens of millions of dollars in profit each year, and have no investors, board, or any plans to ever raise money or sell the company. In our conversation, we explore a path many tech founders never consider—bootstrapping. We discuss: • Why he and his team prioritize profit above all else
guestBioOfficial.zh: 杰森·弗里德是37signals（Basecamp和HEY的开发商）的联合创始人兼CEO。37signals是一家非常与众不同的公司。员工不足80人，却拥有超过10万名客户，每年创造数千万美元利润，没有投资者、董事会，也无意融资或出售公司。在对话中，我们探讨了一条许多科技创始人从未考虑过的道路——自力更生。我们讨论：•为何他和团队将利润置于首位

title.en: Jason Fried challenges your thinking on fundraising, goals, growth, and more
title.zh: 杰森·弗里德挑战您对融资、目标、增长等的认知

summary.en: Jason makes the case that bootstrapping gives founders far more practice at the fundamental skill of making money, and that there's far more room to build a successful, fulfilling, even more lucrative business outside the 'go big or go home' VC path that almost nobody actually wins. He argues constraints like small teams and less cash often produce better outcomes, that gut and instinct are underrated decision tools, that long-term planning is often a mistake, and that work shouldn't feel like war. The episode is a compelling alternative philosophy for building a company on your own terms.
summary.zh: Jason 提出，自筹资金让创始人更多地练习“赚钱”这一根本技能，而且相比几乎无人胜出的“不成功便成仁”的 VC 路线，在它之外有更大的空间去打造成功、充实、甚至更赚钱的事业。他主张小团队、少现金之类的约束往往带来更好的结果，直觉是被低估的决策工具，长期规划常常是错误，工作不应像战争。这期节目是关于“按自己的方式”打造公司的、令人信服的另一种哲学。
